AARE is an open-source reimplementation of the phone side of Android Auto: it speaks the Android Auto projection protocol directly to the car\'s head unit, draws the car screen itself, and runs navigation, media and messaging apps without needing Google Play Services.
Fix a specific car\'s density or visible-area margins without a new build. Edit vehicles.json with a file manager, matching the car by make/model/name.

Fixes AARE ships for specific head units: no wireless where it fails, video size, navigation voice, electric cars, screen pixel shape, the Exit label. Off: every car works as before. A vehicles.json rule can turn them on for one car (builtInFixes).
Override vehicles.json\'s quirks for one car: the head unit connected last. Automatic keeps what the built-in car fixes and your vehicles.json say for it. Other cars are not affected.
Connect to a car once: its quirks can then be changed here.
On: lay the car UI out at the head unit\'s reported pixel ratio, from protocol 1.2 (vehicles.json can still ask for a specific ratio either way). Off: always square pixels.
On: keep vehicles.json\'s list of resolutions to pick from, when it has one for this car. Off: pick from everything the head unit offers.
On: send navigation voice on the music channel and leave the guidance channel unused. Off: use the guidance channel normally.
On: send vehicles.json\'s silent messages (or AARE\'s default) before a music stream starts over Wi-Fi. Off: send none.
On: send vehicles.json\'s silent messages (or AARE\'s default) before a navigation-voice stream starts over Wi-Fi. Off: send none.

On: music keeps playing when the car answers a navigation prompt\'s request with GAIN_TRANSIENT. Off: only navigation voice plays then. A GAIN_TRANSIENT answering the music\'s own request, or sent by the car on its own, always lets music play.
On: an unsolicited guidance-only grant from the car pauses the phone\'s music, which plays again on the car\'s next gain. Off: music keeps playing.

Automatic: connect wirelessly unless the built-in car fixes or your vehicles.json say this head unit can\'t. Allow: connect wirelessly even then. Block: never connect wirelessly to this car; other cars and the Wireless switch are not affected.
On: tell apps the car is electric even if it reports no fuel type or an unknown one. Off: use what the car reports.
On: show the app list\'s Exit to car entry for this car. Off: hide it.
On: send SETUP when the microphone channel opens. Off: never send it.
Try On when the car plays the sound but shows no picture. On: the video\'s SPS/PPS goes out only at the start. Off: before every key frame, as usual. Some head units can\'t decode that.

AARE also runs on Android 6 and 7, but Android 8 is the better-supported baseline. On Android 6 and 7, connection notifications can\'t be put in their own channel, so they can\'t be muted separately from AARE\'s other notices in system settings. Everything else works the same, or falls back to an older method automatically.

One tap grants what is still missing, without each permission\'s own dialog: microphone, location, contacts, call log, calendar, phone calls, nearby devices (Bluetooth, Wi-Fi), local network, notifications and notification access

Through Shizuku (running and allowed for AARE), or by hand in Android Auto\'s app info.

AARE disables Google\'s Android Auto for this user through Shizuku (pm disable-user). It stops running, disappears from the app list and no longer answers when a car connects, so the car always comes to AARE.\n\nNothing is uninstalled and its data stays. Cars, apps or features that need Google\'s Android Auto won\'t work until you enable it again with the button here.
Connect to paired cars over Wi-Fi when they come into Bluetooth range

Built-in head units and aftermarket wireless adapters (plugged into the car\'s USB) expect the phone to answer in different orders. Auto uses the standard order, or the adapter order for a car that last connected with it. Choose Adapter if your wireless adapter won\'t connect; Built-in goes back to the standard order for every car.
Associate a car you already connected to wirelessly: Android then starts AARE when that car\'s Bluetooth connects, even with the phone in a pocket. Android asks you to confirm once per car.
Connect to a car wirelessly once, then come back here to associate it.
Approve the car\'s Wi-Fi with Shizuku

For associated cars, Shizuku answers Android\'s \"connect to device\" question, so it isn\'t asked again. The car\'s network stays AARE\'s own, never the phone\'s internet connection. Needs Shizuku running and AARE allowed in it.

Music or a video pauses while a phone app records (a voice message, an assistant listening), and plays on once it is done. Takes effect at the next connection.

While connected to a car, calls use the phone\'s loudspeaker and microphone instead of the car\'s hands-free link. For wireless adapters or head units whose microphone doesn\'t work. Takes effect from the next connection.

After a call on the phone, or an assistant listening, ask the car for the sound again and play on what it paused. For cars that keep the call\'s sound until asked. Android 12 and later. Takes effect at the next connection.

For calls: when a car the phone isn\'t paired with asks to pair over Android Auto, pair with that car through Shizuku instead of Android\'s dialog, if the code matches the one the car sent. Never any other device. Needs Shizuku running and AARE allowed in it.

Head units check the phone\'s certificate. Open-source head units accept the generated one; cars using Google\'s head unit software only accept a certificate issued by Google, which AARE cannot include. You can import one you have the right to use (PEM certificate + PKCS#8 key, or PKCS#12), or download the one from the latest Android Auto app (from github.com/iscle/android-auto-certificates).
Once a day, never while connected, AARE asks the same repository for a newer certificate and uses it. Either way, AARE warns two weeks before Google\'s certificate expires.
Cars that only accept it will refuse AARE. Tap to download a newer one.

Smart-home buttons and values in the car, over MQTT or HTTP
Show home actions in the car
A Home app and dashboard card. AARE connects to your servers only while the car screen is on.

Actions are buttons that publish an MQTT message or send an HTTP request (open the garage, switch the lights on). Tiles show a value from an MQTT topic or an HTTP reply. Home Assistant works through its REST API, a webhook or MQTT.

Passwords, tokens and header values are kept in a private file of their own, not with the other settings, and never written to the connection log. TLS connections check the server\'s certificate against the phone\'s trusted certificates. Plain http:// is refused unless the HTTP server\'s \"Allow plain http on my home network\" is on, and then works only with addresses on your home network.
Addresses starting with / go here, e.g. https://homeassistant.example.org:8123
Sent as \"Authorization: Bearer …\", to this server only (Home Assistant: a long-lived access token from your profile)
Leave empty to keep the saved token

Allow plain http on my home network

Off by default. Lets http:// addresses on your home network work (192.168.…, 10.…, name.local). Not encrypted: anyone on that network can read the requests, the token included. Other addresses always need https://.
